2. The suit was filed seeking reliefs (a) title to the "property described in the schedule-A attached to the plaint, (b) a decree' for khas possession in respect of the property described in schedule-B which is part of the property described in schedule 'A' and (c) for declaration that the deed No.16157 dated %27.10.1969 in favour of Ali Ahmed Khandker and the deed No.16158 dated 27.10.1969 in favour of Wali Mohammad Siddiqui said to have been executed by Jatindra Mohan Roy @ Sachindra Mohan Roy as described in schedule 'C' are forged, nul and void, fabricated and the deeds 'executed and registered by Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui in favour of the defendant Nos.1 and 2 are illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiff (the last relief Was inserted in pursuant to the order of the Court dated November 19, 1988 allowing prayer for amendment of the plaint). The application seeking amendment of the plaint was filed on July 10, 1988: 

 31. The plaintiff has prayed for declaration of title stating that his cause for seeking such relief arose on October 27, 1969. As stated earlier the suit was filed on September 3, 1976. In the background .of the aforesaid fact the relief so sought was barred in view of the provision of Article 120 of the Limitation Act. The other relief i.e. relief b(I) was also barred under Article 120 of the Limitation Act in the background of the fact stated hereinbefore. It may be mentioned that the relief's (a) and (b) i.e. declaration of title in respect of the property in schedule 'A' and recovery of khas possession of the property described in schedule 'B' are independent reliefs and as such in case the relief as regard declaration of title if is found to be barred then there is no question of granting relief as to recovery of possession of the property (in 'B' schedule) which is part of the property in respect whereof declaration of title has been sought. It has been submitted by the learned Counsel for the appellants that plaintiff has elected for the relief as in prayer (b)(I) since in the absence thereof he cannot have the complete relief in the suit and as such keeping the said aspect of the matter in view he proceeded with the suit seeking relief in respect of the deeds dated October 27, 1969 (Exts.9 and 9 'ka'). The relief's so sought as has already been found are barred since no case was made out in the pleading nor evidence was led to claim exemption from law of limitation. In reply to the submission of the appellants' learned Counsel on the point of limitation as regard the relief as in (b) (I) i.e. declaration in respect of the deeds dated 27.10.1969 (Exts. 9 and 9 'ka') it has been submitted by the learned Counsel of the plaintiff-Respondent that said relief was redundant as without seeking the said relief the suit could be proceeded and could have the relief's sought in prayer (a) and (b) since in making decision as to the relief's (a) and (b) the documents dated 27.10.1969 (Exts.9 and 9 'ka') would have been an issue and as such plaintiffs suit is not liable to be dismissed or in other words plaintiff cannot be disentitled to have the reliefs as in prayer (a) and (b) i.e. declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. It has also been submitted by the learned Counsel for the plaintiff Respondent that the cause of action as has been stated in the plaint is in no way related to the plaintiffs case of dispossession and that the same at best be referred to the two documents as regard which relief has been sought in prayer (b)(I). The learned Counsel continued that plaintiff has stated his case of dispossession from the 'B' schedule land in paragraphs 6 and 7 of the plaint. It may be mentioned in paragraph 6 of the plaint it has been stated that plaintiff left the area where the property situates in 1968 when law and order situation deteriorated there and in paragraph 7 it has been stated that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are occupying portion of the property in suit described in schedule 'B' since after liberation of the country. It may be mentioned no specific date of dispossession has been stated in the plaint. The learned Counsel upon referring to the averments made in paragraphs 6 and 7 of the plaint has submitted that as in the absence of relief (b) (I) the suit could be proceeded and that the relief as to recovery of possession as is not barred by limitation and consequently as the suit is not liable to fail on the ground of limitation the trial Court as well as the High Court Division had correctly held that the suit was not barred by limitation. It may be mentioned relief sought for declaration of title upon making the averment that the cause of action for filing the suit arose on October 27; 1969 was certainly barred by limitation since suit was filed on September 3, 1976. The learned Counsel for, the plaintiff-Respondent tried to take out the suit from the precincts of limitation upon referring to the provision of Article 4 of the Bangladesh (Legal Proceedings) Order, 1972 (President's Order No.12 of 1972). The provision of Article 4 reads as: 

 35. The plaintiff, whose identity was seriously challenged, filed the suit seeking declaration of title in respect of the property in suit and for khas possession of the part of the suit property described in schedule 'B' attached to the plaint. The suit was filed on September 3, 1976. On July 10, 1988 the plaintiff filed an application seeking amendment of the plaint by way of insertion of some facts and the relief (b)(I) i.e. seeking declaration that the kabalas (Exts.9 and 9 `ka') dated October 27, 1969 in the name of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui were forged, fraudulent and" not binding upon the plaintiff. Although aforesaid declaration was sought but the recipients of the said kabalas i.e. Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui were not impleaded in the suit. In that state of the matter it was the consistent contention of the appellants that the suit was bad for defect of parties for non-impleading the said 2 (two) persons. It may be mentioned that appellants while filed the written statement in February 1977 averred that the suit was bad for defect of party for non-impleading the Government of Bangladesh as well as Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui, the vendors of the contesting defendants. The plaintiff added the Government of Bangladesh in the category of defendants. It appears from the record of the suit that interrogatory was served on the defendants to furnish address of the persons who were not made party in the suit and defendants having not replied thereto the plaintiff filed an application with the prayer for debarring them from raising the plea of defect of party and the Court allowed the said prayer. The plaintiff filed an application seeking amendment of the plaint on July 10, 1988. The Court by the order dated November 19, 1988 allowed the prayer for amendment of the plaint and thereupon, amongst others, additional relief (b)(I) was inserted in the plaint seeking declaration that the deeds of 27th October, 1969 in the name of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui were forged, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff. On the incorporation of relief (b) (I) the suit under went transformation making it obligatory for plaintiff, to implead the recipients of Exts.9 and 9 (ka) since those vendees became necessary parties and in their absence no legally sustainable decree be passed against them. On the incorporation of relief (b) (I) as the suit assumed the character different from pre-amendment the order debarring defendants from raising plea of defect of party passed prior to the amendment of plaint incorporating relief (b) (I) lost its force since with the amendment of plaint the vendees of Exts.9 and 9 (ka) who prior to amendment were neither necessary nor proper party, became necessary party and their particulars were very much available in Exts:9 and 9 (ka).
